title: mesh_authz plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `mesh_authz` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component MeshAuthzConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

MeshAuthzAction.description:
Istio `spec.action`, required on every rule. There is deliberately NO
default: a rule whose action failed to deserialize used to fall back to
`allow`, turning an operator's DENY into a grant with no diagnostic.

`custom` delegates to a `meshConfig.extensionProviders` entry carried on
the mesh slice. A provider name that does not bind — and every `custom`
rule in a flat `mesh_policies` config, which has no provider source at
all — refuses with a fixed `403` that no provider's `failOpen` admits.

MeshAuthzConditionMatch.description:
One Istio `when[]` condition. At least one of `values` / `not_values`
must be non-empty; a condition with neither never matches and is
rejected at admission. Keys outside the documented Istio set are
rejected with a field-specific diagnostic so a DENY condition on an
unmodelled attribute cannot silently fail open. See `docs/mesh.md` →
"Condition keys" for the key set and the per-key value grammars.

MeshAuthzConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_authz — Layer 2 mesh authorization evaluator. Applies
Istio-style `MeshPolicy` (ALLOW / DENY / AUDIT) rules to the SPIFFE
identity extracted by `spiffe_identity` or the HBONE baggage on
ambient mTLS streams. DENY rules are evaluated first (first match
wins); the presence of any ALLOW rule with no match triggers an
implicit deny.
`to.hosts` / `notHosts` match normalized literal request authorities,
without service-alias expansion. Explicit decimal ports use one
canonical spelling on both request and pattern sides; wildcard ports
remain supported. Signed request ports are rejected at admission.

Source matching enforces both the positive identity matchers
(`principals` in Istio `<trust-domain>/ns/.../sa/...` form,
`serviceAccounts`, `namespaces`, `trustDomains`,
`requestPrincipals`) and the conjunctive negative and IP-block
matchers (`notPrincipals`/`notServiceAccounts`/`notNamespaces`/
`notTrustDomains`/`notRequestPrincipals`/`ipBlocks`/`notIpBlocks`/
`remoteIpBlocks`/`notRemoteIpBlocks`). `when:` conditions cover the
complete documented Istio condition-key set: `source.principal`,
`source.namespace`, `source.serviceAccount`, `source.trustDomain`,
`source.ip`, `remote.ip`, `destination.ip`,
`destination.port`, `connection.sni`, `request.auth.principal`,
`request.auth.presenter`, `request.auth.audiences`,
`request.auth.claims[...]` string or string-list values including
nested claim leaf paths, `request.headers[...]`, and
`experimental.envoy.filters.<filter>[<key>]`.
Dynamic header/claim keys follow Istio's loose map-key framing: the
first `[` and final `]` delimit a non-empty interior without a separate
HTTP-header-name parse. Known HTTP pseudo-headers (`:authority`,
`:method`, `:path`, `:scheme`) are sourced from typed request facts;
unusual admitted interiors that cannot materialize remain absent.
Values follow Istio's string-matcher grammar (`*` presence,
`<prefix>*`, `*<suffix>`, otherwise exact — a mid-string `*` is literal
text) for every key EXCEPT the ones Istio compiles differently:
`source.ip`/`remote.ip`/`destination.ip` are CIDR blocks;
`source.serviceAccount` is an exact match over
`<namespace>/<service-account>` where a bare `<service-account>` is
resolved against the declaring policy's namespace and a `*` is rejected;
and `source.namespace` treats every `*` as an arbitrary substring at any
position, including mid-string and repeated stars. Keys outside the
documented prefixes — and empty/oversized/control-character keys or
malformed values, non-numeric
`destination.port` values, malformed IP CIDRs, a `source.serviceAccount`
with a `*` or more than one `/`, a `source.trustDomain` with a `/` or a
repeated/mid-string `*`, a non-ASCII `connection.sni` value that
cannot be converted to its A-label, and collections over 64 `when[]`
entries per
rule or 256 values per list (16 values of at most 320 bytes for
`source.serviceAccount`) — are rejected during translation/config
validation with a field-specific diagnostic, on both `values` and
`notValues`, so DENY conditions cannot silently fail open.
`connection.sni` values are normalized at load to the spelling of the
received ClientHello SNI: one trailing dot is stripped, ASCII is
lowercased, and a non-ASCII (U-label) name is converted to its A-label
with IDNA. Other ASCII characters that DNS hostnames do not allow are
not rejected; such a value never matches.
An attribute the path CAN source but that this request lacks follows
ordinary Istio semantics (a `values` check fails; a `notValues`-only
check passes). An attribute the path can NEVER source — an HTTP-only key
on a TCP/UDP/DTLS connection, a source/remote/destination IP or
destination port with no typed transport evidence, or any
`experimental.envoy.filters.*` key — is fail-closed in
both directions, matching Istio's non-HTTP-port behavior: a DENY rule
ignores the field and still matches, while an ALLOW or AUDIT rule can
never match. `destination.ip` is sourced only from the captured pre-NAT
original destination or the connection's local address, never from a
client-settable header. That mesh-authz connection fact is separate
from VirtualService L4 `destinationSubnets`, which accepts only trusted
PROXY/capture original-destination evidence and never an ordinary
listener's bind/local address.
Negative identity matchers reject only when the source/JWT identity
is present and matches an excluded pattern; absent identities satisfy
the negative matcher so DENY policies such as `notPrincipals: ["*"]`
and `notRequestPrincipals: ["*"]` catch anonymous traffic. IP-block
matchers fail closed when the IP they test is absent, and malformed
CIDRs reject translated resources or direct plugin config. See
`docs/mesh.md`.

Auto-injected by mesh mode on every applicable topology; reserved
plugin id `__mesh_authz`. PolicyScope filtering (`MeshWide` /
`Namespace` / `WorkloadSelector` / `TargetRefs`) is applied at
construction time from the slice-embedded workload identity, except in
node-waypoint topology where the filter runs per-request against the
pod-scoped cache attached to `RequestContext`. `TargetRefs`
(AuthorizationPolicy `spec.targetRef` / `spec.targetRefs`) is
waypoint-only and is additionally re-checked per request against the
exact destination Service and waypoint Gateway/GatewayClass identity — construction-time
retention is OR over the attachment list and never widens a targeted
policy onto another destination. See `docs/mesh.md`.

Root-shape admission: an object, or `null` (how an omitted `config:`
block deserializes for every plugin, meaning "no configuration
supplied"). A scalar or array root is REJECTED at construction rather
than degraded into a default instance — a policy-free `mesh_authz`
never raises the implicit-deny floor and therefore allows every
request. Unknown root keys are rejected for the same reason.

mesh_slice.description:
Embedded mesh slice — supplied by mesh-mode auto-injection.
Carries the filtered policy set plus the workload's
`namespace`/`labels` used for slice-level scope filtering, the
admitted `ext_authz_providers` set, and the destination inventory.
Not intended for direct operator configuration; operator-managed
instances pass `mesh_policies` instead.

Deliberately left unmodelled here. The slice is a machine-authored
document produced by the same Ferrum build that consumes it, its
shape tracks every mesh resource family, and a partial schema for
it would drift into rejecting valid injected configuration. It is
admitted by the runtime deserializer instead, which fails the whole
plugin generation on a malformed slice so the previous valid
generation keeps serving. Its root members are closed (an
unrecognized top-level slice member is rejected), and its
`mesh_policies` member follows the same closed policy grammar
modelled below, including the never-match matcher refusals.

Its `ext_authz_providers` entries are closed (with their
`include_additional_headers_in_check` and
`include_request_body_in_check` objects) and may declare
`headers_to_upstream_on_allow` (provider response headers that
replace the backend request's same-named headers on an allowed
CUSTOM check, applied in this plugin's `before_proxy`; client copies
are always removed) and `headers_to_downstream_on_allow` (added to
the allowed response in `after_proxy`, `Set-Cookie` appended).
Gateway identity assertions (`x-consumer-*`, `x-path-param-*`, …),
`content-*`, and (upstream) `set-cookie` are refused there. Every
check carries `x-ferrum-source-principal`,
`x-ferrum-source-namespace`, `x-ferrum-source-service-account`, and
`x-ferrum-request-principal`.

mesh_policies.description:
Standalone-mode policy list. Used by direct configuration when no
slice is available. Rules with `action: custom` in this form always
DENY: a flat list carries no `extensionProviders` source, and a
delegation that cannot be executed is never allowed to fall through
to the ALLOW/DENY tiers.

The grammar is CLOSED at every level and `action` is REQUIRED on
every rule: each misspelling here removes a restriction the
operator wrote, so an unrecognized member fails admission rather
than silently widening the effective policy.

namespace.description:
Proxy workload namespace, used by the slice-level PolicyScope
filter to discard policies that do not apply to this workload.
Overrides any namespace embedded in `mesh_slice`.

labels.description:
Proxy workload labels, used by the slice-level scope filter for
`WorkloadSelector`-scoped policies. Overrides any labels embedded
in `mesh_slice`.

trust_domain_aliases.description:
Additional SPIFFE trust domains accepted as equivalent to the
peer cert's trust domain when authorising HBONE baggage
`source.principal`. Empty (default) means strict same-trust-domain
match. `null` is accepted and treated as absent. Each entry must be
a valid SPIFFE trust domain (SPIFFE-ID section 2.1): lowercase, at
most 255 bytes, and composed only of `[a-z0-9._-]`, including at
the first and last byte.

per_pod_policy_scoping.description:
When `true`, the construction-time slice-level scope filter is
skipped and policies are filtered per-connection using the
`PolicyScopeCache` attached to `RequestContext.node_waypoint_policy_scope`
(HTTP/HBONE) or `StreamConnectionContext.node_waypoint_policy_scope`
(raw TCP streams). A connection whose source pod has no resolved
per-pod scope records `mesh_authz.scope_missing`; when any
namespace/selector-scoped policy is configured it then **fails closed**
(`403`, `mesh_authz.deny_policy=scope_missing`) on the HTTP/HBONE
request path and raw TCP streams (at accept) — a missing scope
means the source workload left the live slice generation, not an
enrollment race, so a long-lived connection from a removed workload
stops being served under scoped authz. NodeWaypoint UDP/DTLS has no
trustworthy per-datagram/session pod scope, so slice preparation
disables UDP/DTLS service/proxy paths when enforcing
namespace/selector-scoped policies are present; mesh-wide UDP/DTLS
policy remains evaluable, and audit-only scoped policy does not
force suppression. Auto-set by mesh injection on `NodeWaypoint`
topology where one listener serves many pods.

ambient_udp_source_scoping.description: Enables node-waypoint Ambient UDP source-policy scoping. Injected by mesh runtime configuration rather than operator-managed plugin config.

cluster_domain.description: Primary Kubernetes cluster domain injected by mesh mode.

cluster_domains.description: Deduplicated cluster-domain aliases used for node-waypoint service host matching; injected by mesh mode.

node_waypoint_route_upstreams.description: Mesh-generated route upstream metadata used to precompute destination policy scopes for node-waypoint dispatch. Each entry and each target is closed: an unrecognized member is rejected.

node_waypoint_route_branches.description: Mesh-generated candidate destinations of each NodeWaypoint VirtualService route whose `mesh_route_dispatch` rules can select a destination other than the route's own: the route's own destination first, then each rule destination. Each candidate's destination policy is evaluated before dispatch, and the destination a request finally reaches is admitted only on its own verdict. Every entry and destination is closed; a destination names exactly one of `upstream_id` or `backend_host` + `backend_port`. A weighted split the route dispatches leg by leg (`mesh_route_dispatch` `weighted_splits`, issue #7387) is listed through its legs, never as a candidate of its own.

weighted_split.description:
The route reaches some candidates only through
weighted-split leg selection, so verdicts are recorded even
when no AuthorizationPolicy is loaded and a split no leg was
selected for is refused.

own_is_weighted_split.description:
The route's own destination (the first entry) is a weighted
split: it is never judged or admitted, and each selected
leg's own verdict decides.

trusted_hbone_assertors.description:
Allow-list of identity-asserting infrastructure components whose
HBONE baggage `source.principal` may rewrite the authz principal.
Bare service-account names match any peer whose SPIFFE path ends
with `/sa/<name>`; full SPIFFE IDs match exactly. Default is
`["ztunnel", "waypoint"]`. Explicit empty array disables all
baggage rewriting.

Matching a peer is necessary but NOT sufficient (issue #4274):
every entry also carries a grant that decides WHICH identities that
peer may assert. String entries and objects without `asserts` /
`scope` grant `same_namespace` only, so a peer in
`ns/attacker/sa/waypoint` can no longer assert
`ns/prod/sa/payments`. Baggage refused by the grant is dropped, the
peer-cert identity is used instead, and the request is stamped
`mesh_authz.ignored_baggage.assertion_out_of_scope=true`.

MeshAuthzPolicy.description:
One `MeshPolicy` document, as accepted by the `mesh_authz` plugin's
`mesh_policies` list and by the native/file mesh document. Mirrors
Istio `AuthorizationPolicy`.

The grammar is CLOSED at every level below: an unrecognized member is
rejected at admission rather than dropped, because every misspelling in
an authorization grammar removes a restriction. See `docs/mesh.md` →
"MeshPolicy" and "Rule Matching".

Matchers that could never match are rejected at plugin construction
too — for the flat `mesh_policies` form and an embedded `mesh_slice`
alike, with the same diagnostics as the native mesh validator: an
empty `name` / `namespace`, an empty `from[{}]` or `to[{}]` entry, a
`to.headers` pseudo-header, an invalid `hosts` / `not_hosts` pattern,
and an inadmissible `port_patterns` / `not_port_patterns` entry.

name.description: Policy name, used in deny diagnostics and metadata.

namespace.description:
The namespace that declared this policy. Load-bearing beyond
identification: a bare `source.serviceAccount` value in a `when`
condition is resolved against it.

rules.description:
Rules are additive. DENY rules are evaluated first and the first
match wins; if any ALLOW rule is loaded and none matches, the
implicit-deny floor refuses the request. An explicitly empty list
is a valid scaffold that matches nothing.

MeshAuthzPolicyScope.description:
Which workloads this policy applies to, discriminated by `kind`.
Resolved by the shared `policy_scope_applies_to_workload` predicate at
plugin construction — except in node-waypoint topology, where one
listener serves many pods and the filter runs per request against the
pod-scoped cache.

Closed like the rest of the grammar: each `kind` admits only its own
members, so an unrecognized sibling key (including one beside
`kind: mesh_wide`) is rejected at admission. The nested `selector` and
every `attachments` entry are closed too.

namespace.description: Applies to workloads in exactly this namespace.

selector.description:
Label/namespace selector. An empty selector matches EVERY
workload, which is why unknown members are rejected here: a
misspelled `labels` key would widen a targeted policy onto the
whole mesh instead of failing admission.

attachments.description:
Istio `spec.targetRefs` attachments. A policy matches when ANY
attachment applies (OR), and retention alone proves nothing —
every runtime consumer re-checks the exact attachment against
its own authoritative evidence. Waypoint-only.

MeshAuthzPrincipalMatch.description:
One source identity matcher. Every populated field must match. A source
with no verified peer identity never matches.

spiffe_id_pattern.description:
Glob over the Istio source principal
(`<trust-domain>/ns/<ns>/sa/<sa>`); a full `spiffe://…` pattern is
also accepted in direct config.

namespace_pattern.description: Glob over the source workload namespace.

trust_domain_pattern.description: Glob over the source trust domain.

MeshAuthzRequestMatch.description:
One request matcher (Istio `to[].operation`). Positive and negative
fields in the SAME matcher are conjunctive — never split a negative
field into a separate rule.

ALLOW/AUDIT rules fail closed when the attribute is absent. DENY and
`custom` rules treat an UNSOURCEABLE attribute as a match (Istio's
non-HTTP-port model), but an HTTP-family request whose header map was
parsed and simply lacks the named header is ABSENT, not unsourceable,
and fails a positive `headers` predicate for every action.

paths.description: Glob patterns, matched against the canonical policy path.

hosts.description:
Glob patterns over the normalized literal request authority. These
do NOT expand service aliases.

port_patterns.description: Istio string-match ports such as `"*"` or `"8*"`.

headers.description:
Header name (case-insensitive, lowercased at config load) to glob
value pattern. The pseudo-header names `:path`, `:method`,
`:authority`, and `:scheme` are rejected (they are not in the
request header map; use `paths` / `methods` / `hosts`, or a
`when: request.headers[:path]` condition). A header sent as several
field lines is matched as ONE value — every line joined with `, `
(`; ` for `cookie`) — the same reading `when: request.headers[...]`
conditions and CUSTOM forwarded headers use.

MeshAuthzRule.description:
One authorization rule. Every populated dimension must match (a
conjunction); within a dimension the entries are ORed.

request_principals.description:
Glob patterns over the JWT-derived `{issuer}/{subject}` request
principal. HTTP-only: on a Layer-4 session a DENY/`custom` rule
ignores it and an ALLOW/AUDIT rule can never match on it.

not_request_principals.description:
Conjunctive negative match over the request principal. An absent
principal SATISFIES it, which is how `["*"]` catches anonymous
HTTP traffic.

never_matches.description:
Synthetic marker for a rule that must affect policy accounting but
never match traffic — Istio's ALLOW-without-rules "allow nothing".
Set by translation; hand-authoring it is not useful.

MeshAuthzSourceNegation.description:
Conjunctive negative-identity and IP-block matchers for one Istio
`from[].source`. These AND with the ORed positive `from` list; placing
them in `from` would let traffic through whenever a single negative-only
entry matched.

Negative identity matchers succeed when the identity is ABSENT, which is
how `not_spiffe_id_patterns: ["*"]` catches anonymous traffic. IP-block
matchers fail CLOSED when the IP they test is absent.

ip_blocks.description: CIDR or bare IP (host route); matched against `source.ip`.

remote_ip_blocks.description: CIDR or bare IP; matched against XFF-derived `remote.ip`.

MeshTrustedHboneAssertors.description:
Trusted HBONE assertor allow-list shared by `mesh_authz`,
`workload_metrics`, and the injected
`_effective_mesh_authz_baggage_gates`. Both plugins admit it through one
parser, so this one schema is the contract for every copy. `null` (or
omission) selects the default `["ztunnel", "waypoint"]`; `[]` disables
baggage-derived identity entirely.

Whitespace is trimmed with Rust `str::trim` (Unicode `White_Space`)
before any comparison; the patterns spell that class out explicitly so
every JSON Schema regex dialect reads it the same way. A value that is
empty after trimming is refused.

asserts.description:
Exact SPIFFE IDs this assertor may assert and nothing
else — the inventory of workloads it actually fronts. An
empty array authorizes nothing. `null` is treated as
absent. Mutually exclusive with `scope`.

scope.description:
Explicit grant contract. `same_namespace` (the default
for every entry) permits only identities in the
assertor's own Kubernetes namespace; `mesh_wide` requires
`assertor` to be a full, exactly matched `spiffe://` ID,
permits any identity that clears the trust-domain gate,
and logs a warning at construction. Mutually exclusive
with `asserts`. `null` is treated as absent. Surrounding
whitespace is trimmed before the value is compared,
matching the `assertor` field's normalization; the
pattern rather than an `enum` is what expresses that.

assertor.description:
Bare service-account name (matches any peer whose SPIFFE path ends
with `/sa/<name>`) or full `spiffe://` SPIFFE ID (matches exactly)
identifying the peer this entry admits. Surrounding whitespace is
trimmed before matching.
